mainEntity.name: How much does a Volkswagen T-Roc R 2.0 TSI engine replacement cost in the UK?

acceptedAnswer.text: A Volkswagen T-Roc R engine replacement typically costs £3,200-£5,500 for a rebuilt unit supply-only, with fitted prices ranging from £4,500-£7,500 depending on the engine code (DNUE vs CZPB) and labour rates. 4Motion system calibration is included in specialist fitting. Used engines: £1,500-£4,200. Reconditioned: £2,500-£5,500. Rebuilt with warranty: £3,200-£5,500. Fitting labour: 10-14 hours at £65-£100/hr.

mainEntity.name: What are the signs of fuel injector failure on a Volkswagen T-Roc R?

acceptedAnswer.text: Common signs include rough running, misfires, poor starting, and high fuel usage. Volkswagen has a TPI code (20678014) for this known problem on pre-2022 EA888 engines. Rough running and engine misfires. Poor starting and stalling. High fuel consumption. Severe injector clogging causing inconsistent fuel delivery.

mainEntity.name: Does the Volkswagen T-Roc R have a timing belt or chain?

acceptedAnswer.text: The EA888 2.0 TSI engine in the T-Roc R uses a timing chain, not a belt. The tensioner can fail, particularly on start-up from cold. Rattling noise on cold start is a common symptom of tensioner wear. Timing chain - not a belt. Tensioner failure can cause catastrophic damage. Rattling on cold start: have it inspected immediately. Updated tensioner design improves reliability.

mainEntity.name: What is the most common problem on the Volkswagen T-Roc R?

acceptedAnswer.text: The most common problems are fuel injector failure (pre-2022 models) and water pump/thermostat housing leaks. The injectors can fail due to overheating, while the water pump housing is a known weakness on EA888 engines. Injector failure: pre-2022 engines affected, TPI code 20678014. Water pump/thermostat housing: common leak issue across EA888. Timing chain tensioner: potential catastrophic damage. DSG mechatronic: can fail at higher mileages.

mainEntity.name: Is the Volkswagen T-Roc R 2.0 TSI engine reliable?

acceptedAnswer.text: The EA888 2.0 TSI is a proven, high-performance engine that is 'a really reliable motor in all states of tune'. However, it has known weaknesses - water pumps are an issue, but if you factor that into your budget, the engine is solid. The engine was 'pretty well sorted' by the time the first T-Roc R came out in 2019. Generally reliable with proper maintenance. Water pump issues are the most common weakness. Pre-2022 injector failure is a known concern. Regular servicing is critical for reliability.

mainEntity.name: What's the difference between the T-Roc R engine codes?

acceptedAnswer.text: The T-Roc R uses two main engine codes: DNUE (2019-2023, 300 PS, EA888 Gen 4) and EA888 Evo4 (2024-present, 333 PS). The R-Line 2.0 TSI uses CZPB (190 PS, EA888 Gen 3b). The R models share their powertrain with the Golf R. DNUE: 300 PS, 2019-2023, 7-speed DSG. EA888 Evo4: 333 PS, 2024-present, facelift. CZPB: 190 PS, R-Line only (not R).

historyTimeline.h2: Volkswagen T-Roc R 2.0 TSI 4Motion - Engine History & Specs at a Glance
historyTimeline.intro: The Volkswagen T-Roc R was launched in 2019 as the performance flagship of the T-Roc range, bringing the legendary EA888 2.0-litre turbocharged engine from the Golf R into a compact SUV body. With 300 PS and 400 Nm of torque, it delivers 0-62 mph in just 4.9 seconds and a top speed of 155 mph. The T-Roc R uses Volkswagen's 4Motion all-wheel-drive system and a 7-speed DSG gearbox, sharing its powertrain with the Golf R, Audi SQ2 and Cupra Ateca.

milestones.description: DNUE, 2.0-litre EA888 turbo petrol, 300 PS (221 kW) - launch engine for T-Roc R, 7-speed DSG, 4Motion, 400 Nm torque
2021 - DNUE (continued) - minor ECU updates, same 300 PS output
DNUE with improved injectors - Volkswagen updated the injectors on engines from model year 2022 to address known failure issues
EA888 Evo4 (333 PS) introduced for facelift models - higher power output, revised turbocharger

commonProblems.h2: Volkswagen T-Roc R 2.0 TSI 4Motion Engine Problems - Repair Cost vs Replacement
commonProblems.h3: The Volkswagen T-Roc R's EA888 2.0 TSI engine is a proven, high-performance unit, but it has specific, well-documented issues - particularly around fuel injectors, the water pump/thermostat housing, and the timing chain tensioner. Rebuilt engines through EnginesMarket include upgraded components addressing the original failure point, plus a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty.

problems.h4: Fuel Injector Failure - The Most Common Volkswagen T-Roc R Problem
problems.affectedModels: Volkswagen T-Roc R (DNUE engine, pre-2022 models)
problems.rootCause: Fuel injectors on pre-2022 EA888 engines can fail, with Volkswagen issuing a TPI code (20678014) for this known problem. Volkswagen updated the injectors on engines from model year 2022. The injectors can overheat and seize, leading to rough running, misfires, and potentially catastrophic engine damage.

repairOptions.longevity: May restore function if caught early

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace all four injectors with updated units
If injector failure has caused engine damage

problems.vehicleValueCheck: A typical 2019-2023 T-Roc R is worth £16,000-£35,000. For a sub-£18,000 example, a £1,000-£1,800 injector set replacement is a significant but justifiable repair. If the injectors have caused engine damage, a rebuilt engine with warranty is the safest option.
problems.recommendation: Injector failure is a known issue on pre-2022 T-Roc R engines. If you're experiencing rough running, misfires or poor starting, have the injectors tested immediately. Replacing all four injectors with the updated Volkswagen units (specialist cost £1,000-£1,800) is recommended for high-mileage pre-2022 cars - doing one at a time often costs more in the long run. If the engine has been damaged by injector failure, a rebuilt unit with warranty is the safest option.
problems.cta: -> Compare Volkswagen T-Roc R injector replacement costs

problems.h4: Water Pump & Thermostat Housing Failure - EA888 Weak Point
problems.rootCause: The integrated water pump and thermostat housing on EA888 engines is a common failure item that is prone to leaking. A well-known warranty issue with the EA888 engine thermostat/water pump housing can run a small ongoing leak, particularly on earlier versions 2016-19. The housing can develop slow leaks, overheat the engine, or cause limp mode.

repairOptions.longevity: First step if coolant loss is noticed

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace water pump and thermostat housing
Replace pump, housing, hoses, and flush system
If overheating has caused head gasket or engine damage

problems.vehicleValueCheck: For a T-Roc R worth £16,000-£35,000, a £450-£850 water pump replacement is a justifiable expense if the car is otherwise sound.
problems.recommendation: Water pump and thermostat housing failure is a well-known issue on EA888 engines. If you notice coolant loss, overheating, or warning lights, have the cooling system inspected immediately. The "P" revision of the water pump housing is the latest OEM revision. Specialist replacement at £450-£850 is significantly cheaper than dealer prices. Factor this into your ownership costs - many owners replace the water pump preventatively at 60,000 miles.
problems.cta: -> Compare Volkswagen T-Roc R water pump replacement costs

problems.h4: Timing Chain Tensioner Wear - Volkswagen T-Roc R
problems.affectedModels: Volkswagen T-Roc R (all EA888 variants, particularly earlier engines)
problems.rootCause: The timing chain tensioner can fail, particularly on start-up from cold as the tensioner does not apply the correct pressure (ratchet fails) until the oil pressure activates it. A rattling or clanking noise on cold start is a common symptom. If ignored, the chain can skip, causing pistons to contact valves and resulting in catastrophic engine damage.

repairOptions.longevity: If rattling on startup is heard

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: If chain has skipped causing valve/piston damage
repairOptions.longevity: Catastrophic failure; often the only option

problems.vehicleValueCheck: For a T-Roc R worth £16,000-£35,000, a £1,000-£1,800 timing chain replacement is a sensible preventative investment. If the chain has failed, a rebuilt engine with warranty is the safest option.
problems.recommendation: Timing chain tensioner failure is a known issue on EA888 engines. If you hear a rattling noise on cold start, have the timing chain inspected immediately. Preventative replacement at £1,000-£1,800 specialist cost is far cheaper than a full engine replacement at £3,200-£5,500. The updated tensioner design has improved reliability.
